item.title: Longford man jailed for two years for assaulting train ticket inspector
item.description: A Longford man who assaulted an Irish Rail ticket inspector on a train at Connolly Station has been jailed for two years. Gerry Nevin (32) assaulted the injured party on board a Dublin to Sligo train at Connolly Station after the injured party asked him to leave the train because he had a can of alcohol. item.title: Taoiseach accepts invitation to visit White House on St. Patrick's Day
item.description: The Taoiseach has accepted an invitation to visit the White House on St. Patrick's Day. Micheál Martin last night confirmed he received a formal invitation from US President Donald Trump yesterday. He has been facing calls to boycott the annual tradition in light of President Trump's controversial policies in the US and internationally. item.title: British Army officer who died in live fire training incident to be laid to rest in Co. Roscommon today
item.description: A British Army officer who grew up in Co Roscommon who died following a live fire training incident in England will be laid to rest later today. Captain Gilbert Muldowney, of Ballinameen passed away following the incident at Otterburn Training Area in Northumberland on Sunday, January 25th. Son of David and Meg Muldowney from Ballinameen, Gilbert, was educated locally at Elphin Community College after the family moved from Dublin to the north Roscommon village. item.title: Roscommon nurse completes 23,000km charity cycle to Sydney
item.description: A Roscommon nurse has completed an epic 23,000 kilometre charity cycle after arriving at Sydney Opera House in the early hours of this morning Irish time. Arigna native Fergal Guihen set off from his home in March 2024 and has since cycled through 28 countries. The Rossie to Aussie Cycle is in aid of Mayo Roscommon Hospice and North West STOP. item.title: 13 suppliers providing hot school meals in Co. Roscommon
item.description: 13 suppliers are providing hot school meals in Co Roscommon. The scheme has been available to all primary schools since September. The Social Protection Minister says the School Meals Programme is designed to provide regular, nutritious food to children. Dara Calleary says this supports them to take full advantage of the education provided to them. He says it's also designed to encourage school attendance. item.title: More than 500 applications for retention permission submitted locally since 2024
item.description: More than 500 applications for retention permission have been submitted locally in the last two years. An investigation by the Irish Independent on the "build first, ask for permission later" culture revealed more than half of all retention applications lodged since January 2024 have been approved by local authorities across the country. item.title: LISTEN: 'A role model who died doing what he loved' - army captain's sisters pay moving tribute at his Roscommon funeral
item.description: The sisters of an army captain, from north Roscommon, say their brother was a role model who died doing what he loved. Captain Gilbert Muldowney’s funeral Mass took place in St Attracta’s Church in Ballinameen this afternoon and he was laid to rest afterwards in the adjoining cemetery. item.title: Longford and Roscommon record hurling league wins
item.description: Longford overcame Monaghan to make it three wins from three in the Allianz hurling league division four played at Cloghan. Joe Rabbit, Martin Farrell and Reuben Murray points helped Monaghan into a six point lead after 23 minutes, Longford lading eight points to two. Monaghan were reduced to 14 players on the stroke of half-time when James Brady was shown a red card. Longford took a nine point lead to the break, 12 points to three.
